name: SDK catalog regeneration and discovery keywords (P16 EP-387)
skipReason: Build tooling that emits two data files — no runtime route exists to call. Verified by tests/platform/sdkCatalog.test.ts (47 assertions over the regenerated catalog and index) and by the CI drift gate `node scripts/catalog/regenerate-sdk-catalog.js --check`.
description: Regenerates mcp-server/data/sdk-catalog.json and sdk-catalog-index.json from tests/api_definitions/**, so projexlight_get_sdk_api resolves every endpoint this sprint added. Proves all four criteria. The stakes: the catalog is what an AI coding tool reads to decide reuse-vs-rebuild, so an SDK missing from it is for that purpose an SDK that does not exist — the tool cannot find it and writes the capability again. Endpoints are DERIVED from the api_definitions rather than typed by hand, because those definitions are already the contract and deriving is what stops catalog and reality drifting the moment somebody adds a route. AC1: each catalogued endpoint carries method, path, requiresAuth, payload_shape (field NAMES only — values are bulk that would bloat the artifact), fieldEnums and dependsOn; the auth contract survives into the catalog, including requiresAuth:false on the HMAC-gated lead-form webhook, since a consumer sending a Bearer token to a signature-authenticated endpoint would 401 with no explanation. AC3: sdk_count and api_count are RECOUNTED from the tree rather than incremented, so a hand-edited total cannot drift; the regeneration took the catalog from 67 SDKs / 469 APIs to 85 / 681, revealing it had been stale well beyond this sprint. AC4: the compact index is rebuilt from the catalog minus payloads and held under a 64 KB budget — it loads into a model's context on EVERY discovery call, so its size is a running cost and an index that crowds out the answer defeats its own purpose; it currently sits at ~26 KB. AC2: reuse_when keywords are the words someone WITH THE PROBLEM would type, not the SDK's own vocabulary — a developer about to rebuild SLA tracking types 'response time' or 'escalation', never 'sdk-sla', because if they knew it existed they would not be rebuilding it. QA edge cases: a test asserts every P16 SDK owns at least one keyword no other SDK claims, which is the property that actually makes routing work — some overlap is unavoidable and already widespread (31 pre-existing keywords are shared, e.g. 'escalation' across sdk-handoff and sdk-sla), so what matters is that each SDK has SOME phrase landing on it alone; a failing test caught 'golden record' being claimed by both sdk-projection and sdk-identity-resolver, and it was removed from projection because identity-resolver owns record-level MDM while projection is attribute-level survivorship; INTERNAL_FUNCTION and EVENT_CONTRACT definitions are excluded since they describe no HTTP surface, and the 'platform' pseudo-SDK is excluded because build tooling is not something a vertical installs.

testCases.name: Every P16 SDK is catalogued with full endpoint specs
The auth contract survives into the catalog
Briefed reuse_when keyword sets are present
Distinctive phrases route to exactly one SDK
Counts reconcile and the index stays under budget

errorCases.name: Catalog drift fails the CI gate
errorCases.message: sdk-catalog drift: an endpoint exists in tests/api_definitions that the catalog does not list.
errorCases.when: a route is added with an api_definition but the catalog is not regenerated — `--check` exits non-zero rather than rewriting, because an uncatalogued capability is one the next vertical rebuilds

errorCases.name: An oversized index is refused rather than silently shipped
errorCases.message: index is <n> KB, over the 64 KB budget
errorCases.when: the compact map grows past its budget; the generator exits non-zero and tells the author to trim summaries or keywords rather than raise the limit, because the file is loaded into context on every discovery call
